transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-03-28
Start time: 15:00 PT
Duration: ~62 minutes
Attendees: Maya (Redwood AE), Benji (Redwood SE), Sofia (Redwood CSM), Anika (Lyra Sec), Tom (Lyra Platform), Suresh (CISO), Renee (DevOps), Carlos (QA)

Auto-summary (auto-generated): Post-pen test operational alignment. Focus on prioritization, patch cadence, KMS/encryption questions, and SOC2 evidence requests.

[00:00] Maya: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. I see most folks are here. Quick intro — I'm Maya, AE at Redwood. Benji, do you want to jump in with a quick framing from the SE side?
[00:12] Benji: Yeah hi all. Benji Li, Redwood SE. We read the pen test report you shared — thanks for sending that ahead — and this call is to walk through what we think are pragmatic next steps for remediation, how Redwood can help with patch windows, and then cover the security controls like RBAC, S S O, logging and KMS.
[00:28] Anika: Thanks. Our ask is practical: we need a playbook so Ops can run weekly triage, and we want to limit blast radius for model serving. Also we want to get comfortable with Redwood's audit and encryption story because we'll be moving sensitive PII through the inferencing pipeline.
[00:40] Suresh: I'm interested in timelines and how this maps to our SOC two timeline. We have an audit in July so we need evidence of remediation processes not necessarily fully closed but tracked.
[00:51] Maya: Totally. We'll cover evidence handoff and what can be documented for SOC2. Sofia will help coordinate the artifact exchange.
[00:58] Sofia: Quick note: I'll post a secure link for the remediation tracker after the call.

--- Topics: Pen test highlights and severity breakdown ---
[01:14] Benji: High level from the pen test: there were three critical findings — one around an exposed admin endpoint in your old staging VPC that leaked a token; one medium risk around misconfigured RBAC where service accounts had extra permissions; and a few low-risk info disclosures around open debug logs. The rest are configuration and patching.
[01:36] Tom: The exposed admin endpoint was from an older stack we forgot to decommission. That was patched yesterday but the pen test flagged some sessions and we rotated keys. We still want to formalize the patch cadence so this doesn't recur.
[01:48] Anika: Can you outline what Redwood recommends for a patch cadence for inference fleets? We need to balance latency windows for users.
[01:56] Benji: For model serving we usually recommend a 4-week runway for non-urgent patches, with a faster track for critical CVEs — 48–72 hours for critical, 7 days for high, and weekly for medium/low triage. That aligns with what we've done for other enterprise customers. We can also help automate canary rollouts to avoid global impact.
[02:16] Renee: Is that 48 hours workable — we'd need scheduled maintenance windows.
[02:20] Benji: Yes, maintenance windows plus canary policies. Redwood Dedicated customers often configure step-rollouts: 5% of capacity, monitor latency and error rates, then 25, 50, 100. If rollback triggered, automatic fallback to previous model variant.

--- Audit logs and retention ---
[02:40] Maya: On audit logs: you asked about retention and evidence. Redwood keeps request-level audit logs for X days by default but we can configure long-term retention for enterprise (we can supply an export for SOC2). What format do you need these in?
[02:54] Anika: CSV export is fine but we need to show chain-of-custody and tamper-resistance. Also want to know how logs tie to SSO identities and RBAC changes.
[03:06] Benji: Logs include token/user id mapping if you enable SAML/SSO integration. For Dedicated and Private deployments you can ship logs to your SIEM via our audit-forwarder. The forwarder writes to S3 or your syslog depending on architecture.
[03:20] Suresh: On tamper-resistance — do logs get signed / checksum?
[03:24] Benji: We support writing to an append-only store on customer side; Redwood can provide signed exports. In the Hosted tier we maintain internal integrity checks and can produce signed digests for exports. We'll include the export process in the remediation doc.

--- KMS/encryption / data residency ---
[03:40] Anika: Encryption — we use a KMS and keys for data at rest. We want to ensure KV cache and intermediate tensors aren't written to disk unencrypted and that any persisted caches are under our KMS.
[03:50] Benji: Good callout. For Private deployments you can bring your own KMS/HSM. For Dedicated we have integrations with AWS KMS and customer-managed CMKs. KV cache is in-memory by default; when we persist caches for warmup, it's encrypted using the selected CMK. We'll share the KMS diagram.
[04:08] Tom: Data residency — our regulators require EU residency for some models. How does Redwood enforce regional routing?
[04:13] Maya: We route by policy — you can pin models to region, or set routing rules based on request metadata. For Hosted customers we advertise region selection and for Dedicated you control actual placement. We'll document region routing config.

--- Secure SDLC and pipeline checkpoints ---
[04:30] Carlos (QA): From testing side, what are the recommended SDLC hooks? Should we run static scans on prompts or vet new prompt templates?
[04:36] Benji: SDLC suggestions: require pre-deploy security review for model variants, include automated dependency scanning of container images, require canary test plan with perf and failure injects, and add a post-deploy smoke test that validates audit logging and RBAC changes. You can also add linting rules for prompts that flag PII leakage patterns.
[04:54] Renee: We currently have a 2-week sprint cadence; how does that sync with the 4-week patch runway?
[04:58] Benji: The runway is independent; think of it as the triage window. You can prioritize fixes into sprint work, but critical fixes get out-of-band patches. Our standard playbook includes a triage meeting every week until all high/critical findings are mitigated or have a compensating control.

--- Discussion — triage SLA and prioritization ---
[05:15] Anika: For us, top priority is the admin endpoint exposure and RBAC over-privileged accounts. We also want to set concrete SLAs for remediation so auditors see progress.
[05:22] Suresh: Agreed. We want timestamps showing when an issue was discovered, when mitigation was applied, and when verification occurred.
[05:28] Maya: We can support that with the remediation tracker — it will record discovery date, owner, mitigation steps, verification notes and evidence links.
[05:35] Benji: Example triage SLA we suggest: Critical fix or mitigation within 72 hours with mitigation notes; high within 7 days; medium/low into backlog with scheduled patch week.

--- Technical Q&A (more granular) ---
[05:50] Tom: About RBAC — what granularity do you support for service accounts vs human users? We need to ensure operators cannot escalate to cluster admin via Redwood APIs.
[05:59] Benji: We have role-based scopes at the API route-level — e.g., inference:invoke, model:deploy, model:promote, admin:org. You can map your SAML groups to these roles. For Dedicated/Private deployments we can support custom roles and audit that any change to role mapping emits an audit event.
[06:20] Anika: Does Redwood support SSO with SCIM for automated provisioning?
[06:24] Maya: Yes, SAML SSO + SCIM provisioning are supported for enterprise customers. We'll send the SSO integration guide.

--- Mis-transcriptions / small interruptions ---
[06:35] Speaker 6: (inaudible)
[06:40] Benji: sorry, I missed that — go ahead?
[06:43] Speaker 6: nothing — just confirming the exports are Gzip compressed.

--- Rollouts and Canary plan example ---
[06:50] Benji: Example canary: 5% traffic for 30 minutes with latency and error thresholds, then progressive ramp. We run latency histograms and p95 checks, plus model quality smoke tests using a small held-out prompt set. If p95 increases by more than X ms or error rate > Y% we stop and rollback.
[07:10] Carlos: For quality smoke tests, can Redwood plug into our eval harness?
[07:14] Benji: Yes — we have webhook hooks and simple S3-based artifact reading for evals. We'll coordinate a connector.

--- Evidence and SOC2 asks ---
[07:25] Suresh: For the SOC two audit, what artifacts can Redwood provide?
[07:30] Maya: We can provide: audit log exports, KMS key use logs (where available), SSO/SCIM configs, role mapping exports, and evidence of the remediation tracker. For Dedicated/Private we can give more granular host-level configs if you need them.
[07:44] Anika: We also need the pen test vendor statement of remediation acceptance once fixes are verified.
[07:49] Benji: We'll help coordinate test validation and can sign off on verification steps we ran in Redwood, but final acceptance will come from your pen test vendor. We can also run an internal verification checklist and provide screenshots/log exports.

--- Edge cases and residual concerns ---
[08:05] Renee: What about third-party model artifacts or open-source models that might have risky init code or telemetry?
[08:12] Benji: Good point. Our model onboarding checklist includes a runtime vetting step, license scan, and optional sandboxing for untrusted models. We also recommend using quantized variants where feasible to reduce attack surface.
[08:26] Anika: Any guidance on secret rotation for service accounts? Our current rotation is monthly but the pen test flagged a long-lived token.
[08:33] Benji: Shorter rotation for service tokens is better — we recommend automatic rotation with short TTLs and CI/CD integration for secret injection. For short-lived session tokens we use ephemeral credentials. We'll include a recommended secrets rotation plan in the playbook.

--- Closing and recap ---
[08:50] Maya: Recap — Redwood will: share remediation spreadsheet and deck; provide SSO/SCIM integration guide; provide KMS architecture doc; run a canary benchmark with Benji in two weeks; and provide audit log export instructions. Lyra will: upload SOC2 checklist and logs, confirm patch windows and weekly triage owner, and run initial remediation for critical items.
[09:10] Anika: Sounds good. One procedural ask — can Redwood annotate the remediation tracker with suggested verification artifacts so auditors can find things quickly?
[09:18] Maya: Yes we'll add an Evidence column with recommended artifacts and example exports.
[09:22] Suresh: Let's schedule the follow-up: two weeks for canary, weekly triage until high/critical mitigations are verified.
[09:30] Sofia: I'll send calendar invites and the secure drive links.
[09:33] Renee: One last quick question — does Redwood have a minimum maintenance window? Our ops hours are tight.
[09:37] Benji: No hard minimum; we can do phased deployment in off-peak windows. We'll also document expected token rotations and short-term mitigations that avoid full-scale maintenance.

--- End of recorded Q/A ---
[09:50] (meeting wraps up, informal chatter)
